newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania sees operating margins rising next 2/3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Scania sees operating margins rising next 2/3 yrs.

text.p: Swedish truck maker Scania's managing director Leif Ostling said on Monday the company expected to reach double digit operating margins within the next two to three years.

"We should definitely reach two figure operating margins in the next two to three years as long as the bottom does not go out of the industry," Ostling told a news conference after the company posted its six month results.
For the first half of 1997 Scania's operating margin was 7.5 percent and in the second quarter 7.7 percent.
The goal was still for an operating margin of 13-14 percent, Ostling said.
"We have had this historic average of 13-14 percent and that is what we are striving for. I have no reason to change that goal today," he said.
Ostling said the strong rise in order bookings indicated continuing improvement in operating margins in the future despite price pressure in the European market continuing this autumn.
"We should expect continued price pressure this year but it could start to stabilise in the autumn," he said.
The improvement in margins would start on the costs side but the stronger market could also help prices.
Ostling said there was little difference between operating margins in Europe or Latin America.
